table.text: The sample size was estimated for the primary outcome (the proportion of participants with grade ≥2 adverse events) using the Select Statistics two-proportion calculator, assuming a two-sided significance level of 0.05, 80% power and an anticipated absolute difference of 0.30 between the proportions of participants experiencing grade ≥2 adverse events in the AsSET and placebo groups. After allowing for an anticipated 10% dropout, the target sample size was 81 participants. A total of 81 participants were randomly allocated in a 2:1 ratio to docetaxel-based chemotherapy plus AsSET (n = 54) or docetaxel-based chemotherapy plus placebo (n = 27). The 2:1 allocation ratio was chosen to increase exposure to the investigational product, which had been well tolerated in earlier clinical studies, including in healthy volunteers (18).

text.text: NOTE: This preprint reports new research that has not been certified by peer review and should not be used to guide clinical practice.

QoL Quality of life RECIST Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors SAE Serious adverse event Strengths and limitation of this study Robust design in the form of randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with stratified block randomization provides good internal validity

The study is adequately powered to demonstrate the treatment effect for the underlying assumptions Pharmacokinetic sampling in a subset of participants allows assessment of whether AsSET alters docetaxel exposure, an important concern for herb-drug interactions in integrative oncology.
The study, being limited to docetaxel-based chemotherapy regimens at a single institution, may not be generalizable to other cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen.

The inclusion of patients with multiple solid tumours receiving varied docetaxelbased regimens may lead to heterogeneity in the chemotherapy-related adverse events which could affect the interpretability of pooled results.
The 2:1 allocation reduces statistical efficiency compared with equal allocation.

Docetaxel is widely used for advanced and metastatic solid tumours, but dose limiting toxicities, particularly haematological adverse events, often lead to treatment delays, dose reductions or discontinuation and impair quality of life.

Tinospora cordifolia (Guduchi), long used in Ayurveda for its immunomodulatory and rejuvenating properties, has shown chemoprotective potential in experimental and early clinical studies, but robust randomized evidence is lacking.

This trial evaluates whether adding an aqueous standardized extract of T. cordifolia(AsSET) to docetaxel-based chemotherapy reduces grade ≥2 adverse events and improves quality of life in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumours.

This randomized, double-blind, and placebo-controlled trial designed to evaluate the chemoprotective efficacy of an aqueous standardised extract of Tinospora cordifolia (AsSET) in patients with advanced, recurrent or metastatic solid tumors receiving docetaxel-based chemotherapy.
A total of 81 eligible patients that have provided informed consent were recruited in the study.

Participants were randomized 2:1 to AsSET or placebo using stratified permuted block randomization stratified by planned cumulative docetaxel dose (≤ 225 vs >225 mg/m 2 ) except five participants enrolled before that date were allocated by minimization.

text.text: All participants received standard intravenous docetaxel-based chemotherapy plus oral administration of either AsSET (two 300mg tablets, 600mg, twice daily) or matching placebo, from enrolment until completion of docetaxel-based therapy.
Clinical, laboratory, imaging, and questionnaire based-assessment were performed at baseline, at scheduled interval during treatment and at the final visit.
In consenting participants, blood samples for pharmacokinetics were collected once, at nine timepoints up to 24 hours, in any chemotherapy cycle from cycle 2 onwards.
Adverse events were graded according to CTCAE version 5.0.
The primary outcome is the proportion of patients experiencing grade ≥2 adverse events from first dose to study completion (up to 24 weeks).

Secondary outcomes include quality of life measured by the EORTC QLQ-C30 and the disease-site-specific FACT scale, progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1, haematological and biochemical parameters, and pharmacokinetic parameters.
The database was locked on 17 September 2026 and the locked dataset was transferred to an independent statistician who remains blinded to treatment allocation.
Unblinding has not yet been done and outcome analysis has not started.
Participants data are coded to protect confidentiality, and no participant will be identified in any publication without permission.
The findings from this study will be presented at an academic conference and published in scholarly journals regardless of the findings.

text.text: Treated patients showed reductions in mucositis, fatigue, xerostomia, nausea-vomiting, skin reactions and tastelessness, with the least effect on alopecia, and haemoglobin, leucocyte and platelet counts improved in 68% of treated patients compared with controls.

However, the study was small (56 patients in four groups), did not report actual haematological values, analysed groups before and after treatment without between-group comparison, and did not follow CONSORT reporting guidance.
Taken together, these findings suggest that T. cordifolia may attenuate chemotherapy-related adverse effects, but the evidence comes from small, methodologically limited studies.
To our knowledge, no adequately powered, prospectively registered randomized trial has evaluated a standardised T. cordifolia extract as an adjunct to docetaxel-based chemotherapy.

This trial was designed to address that gap by testing whether adding an aqueous standardised extract of T. cordifolia (AsSET) to docetaxel-based chemotherapy reduces grade ≥2 adverse events and improves quality of life.

Objectives This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial aims to evaluate whether adding a standardized aqueous extract of Tinospora cordifolia (AsSET) to docetaxel-based chemotherapy reduces chemotherapy-related adverse events in patients with advanced, recurrent or metastatic solid tumours.

The primary objective is to compare the incidence of treatment-emergent grade ≥2 adverse events (haematological and non-haematological) between docetaxel-based chemotherapy with add-on AsSET and docetaxel-based chemotherapy with add-on placebo.

The secondary objectives are to compare the two arms with respect to: (i) general and cancerspecific quality of life (QoL); (ii) progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1 (iii) haematological and biochemical parameters and (iv) docetaxel pharmacokinetic parameters.
We hypothesised that add-on AsSET would reduce the proportion of participants with grade ≥2 adverse events compared with placebo.
The study is a randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of AsSET.
It employs a parallel-group design with an unequal allocation ratio of 2:1.
The protocol follows the SPIRIT 2025 reporting guidance (17).
text.formatted: The protocol follows the SPIRIT 2025 reporting guidance <ref type="bibr" target="#b16">(17)</ref>.

text.text: The trial was conducted at ACTREC-Tata Memorial Centre, Navi Mumbai and Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai, with an interventional arm and a control arm.

Participants took the study drug orally twice daily from the day of enrolment until completion of docetaxelbased chemotherapy, so the duration of intervention varied with each participant's chemotherapy schedule; adverse events were followed for up to 24 weeks.

The planned study duration was 30 months (24 months of accrual and 6 months of analysis); enrolment ran from 2 November 2023, after the first approval of the Institutional Ethics Committee, to 21 April 2026.

Accrual exceeded the planned 24 months because several other trials were recruiting from the same departments in parallel; the Institutional Ethics Committee was kept informed through regular continuing review reports.

Patients attending the outpatient departments of the participating institutes who had advanced, recurrent or metastatic solid tumours and were scheduled to start docetaxel, alone or combined with other standard chemotherapeutic drugs, were screened and enrolled.
The clinical site coordinators explained the study procedures, risks, benefits and duration, and written informed consent was obtained before enrolment.

text.text: Participants were discontinued from the trial if they withdrew consent (participation was voluntary and consent could be withdrawn at any time) or for any of the following reasons: a serious adverse event; an increase in the severity of a concomitant chronic disease; a new acute illness; a non-medical event making continuation unavoidably impossible; noncompliance with the protocol; or at the discretion of the study doctors.

Non-compliance was defined as taking less than 80% of study tablets, refusing the protocol investigations, not completing the questionnaires, or attending follow-up visits more than 5 days outside the schedule.
A temporary hold of the study drug on the advice of the treating or Ayurvedic physician for an adverse event was not counted as discontinuation.
The reason for each discontinuation was recorded.

The sample size was estimated for the primary outcome (the proportion of participants with grade ≥2 adverse events) using the Select Statistics two-proportion calculator, assuming a two-sided significance level of 0.05, 80% power and an anticipated absolute difference of 0.30 between the proportions of participants experiencing grade ≥2 adverse events in the AsSET and placebo groups.
After allowing for an anticipated 10% dropout, the target sample size was 81 participants.
A total of 81 participants were randomly allocated in a 2:1 ratio to docetaxel-based chemotherapy plus AsSET (n = 54) or docetaxel-based chemotherapy plus placebo (n = 27).
The 2:1 allocation ratio was chosen to increase exposure to the investigational product, which had been well tolerated in earlier clinical studies, including in healthy volunteers (18).

The efficacy analysis population comprised all randomised participants (intention to treat).

For the primary outcome, the proportion of participants with grade ≥2 adverse events will be compared between arms using the χ² test or Fisher's exact test; the same tests will be used for other categorical variables.

Continuous variables (including quality-of-life scores, haematological and biochemical values, and pharmacokinetic parameters) will be summarised as mean (SD) or median (interquartile range) and compared between arms using the t-test or the Mann-Whitney U test, according to the distribution of the data assessed with the Shapiro-Wilk test.

Progression-free survival will be estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using a stratified log-rank test and a stratified Cox proportional hazards model (Efron's method for ties), with treatment as the single covariate and the randomisation stratification factor as the stratifier, reporting the hazard ratio with 95% CI.
All tests will be two-sided, with P < 0.05 considered significant.

The pharmacokinetic sub-study addresses the clinically important question of a possible herb-drug interaction between AsSET and docetaxel, which has so far been examined only in preliminary in vitro studies (27, 28).

text.text: To our knowledge, this trial is the first prospectively registered, randomized controlled trial to evaluate the chemoprotective efficacy of an aqueous standardized extract of T. cordifolia as an adjunct to docetaxel-based chemotherapy.

If the findings demonstrate a significant reduction in chemotherapy-induced adverse events without attenuation of docetaxel pharmacokinetics or antitumor activity of docetaxel, they would generate robust evidence to support the integration of AsSET into oncology practice.
Results will be reported transparently, whether positive, negative, or inconclusive, to contribute to the evidence on herbal adjuncts in cancer care.

Pregnancy or lactation.InterventionsInterventional arm: Participants received standard intravenous docetaxel-based chemotherapy (docetaxel alone or with other standard anticancer drugs, at the dose prescribed by the treating physician) plus oral AsSET tablets supplied by Pharmanza Herbal Pvt.
Ltd. against a certificate of analysis.
Each tablet contained 300 mg of aqueous standardized T. cordifolia extract.
Participants took two tablets (600 mg) twice daily (1200 mg/day), 12hourly after food with water, including on docetaxel infusion days.
This dose lies within the range used in earlier clinical studies of aqueous T. cordifolia extracts(15, 16, 18).

text.text: Product details: AsSET tablets were round, orange, film-coated tablets, each containing 300 mg of an aqueous extract of the stem of Tinospora cordifolia (wild-crafted, India; extraction solvent water; herb-to-extract ratio 10:1).

According to the manufacturer's specification, the extract contained not less than 5% total bitters, 20% total polysaccharides and 0.7% of the sum of four marker compounds (magnoflorine, 20-β-hydroxyecdysone, tinosporide and columbin), and the specification included an HPLC identification test.
All participants received AsSET from a single batch (PHPL/RD/094/CT-102-01), manufactured on 26 August 2023 by Pharmanza Herbal Pvt.
Ltd., Gujarat, India.

A herbarium voucher specimen of the raw plant material was not available to the study team.Control arm: Participants received the same chemotherapy plus placebo tablets, also supplied by Pharmanza, identical to AsSET tablets in colour, size, shape, texture, smell and taste.
Each placebo tablet contained 230 mg of starch (IP) with excipients, and all placebo came from a single batch (PHPL/RD/094/CT-103-01) manufactured on 26 August 2023.
The initial shelf life of the study medication (AsSET and placebo) was 3 years from manufacture.
When this ended in August 2026, the manufacturer reported that it had re-tested the batches and extended the shelf life by one year, and the same batches continued to be dispensed.
Dose modification and interruption: AsSET and placebo doses were not modified for the duration of the study.
The dose of docetaxel, other chemotherapy and supportive drugs was individualized according to the usual schedule for each drug.
AsSET or placebo could be temporarily held on the advice of the treating or Ayurvedic physician.
